text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating Julian Palmer, an 8-year-old boy whom I have been following for recent inflammatory and hematologic changes. He lives with his parents, does well in elementary school, and takes only PRN loratadine for seasonal allergies.

Julian recently presented with lower extremity palpable purpura. A punch biopsy confirmed small-vessel vasculitis, showing a marked superficial perivascular inflammatory infiltrate in the dermis. Concurrently, routine blood counts revealed an absolute neutrophil count down to 780/mcL alongside thrombocytopenia with platelets of 82,000/uL. His red cell indices are entirely preserved, with no pancytopenia. Bone marrow evaluation and peripheral flow cytometry ruled out both B-cell and T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemias. Further immunological workup demonstrated antinuclear antibody positivity at a titer of 1:320. Detailed B-cell paneling showed a reduced proportion of class-switched memory B cells, though unswitched memory B cell populations are not decreased. The CD4:CD8 ratio is normal and not inverted. His circulating immunoglobulin concentrations are not decreased, and complement levels for both C3 and C4 are normal rather than decreased.

Julian has no history of recurrent infections, sepsis, recurrent meningitis, or recurrent oral herpes outbreaks. His gastrointestinal history is unremarkable, with no chronic diarrhea. Baseline chest imaging was clear, showing no lung abscess, invasive pulmonary aspergillosis, or Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Abdominal and lymph node examinations were entirely normal. 

Given these cytopenias, autoimmune serology, and biopsy-proven vascular inflammation, I would be grateful for your formal assessment and recommendations on next steps.

Sincerely,
Dr. Eleanor Vance
